title: Feedback, Outreach and Reporting Entities
summary: How FIUs improve reporting quality through case-specific and general feedback, guidance and outreach, and work with supervisors to address persistent weaknesses in reporting sectors.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How FIUs improve reporting quality through case-specific and general feedback, guidance and outreach, and work with supervisors to address persistent weaknesses in reporting sectors.
Learning Objectives: Design effective general and case-specific feedback to reporting entities
Identify under-reporting and poor-quality reporting by sector
Coordinate with supervisors on reporting compliance
Syllabus: Forms of feedback: case-specific, sectoral and typology-based
Guidance, red-flag indicators and outreach programmes
Measuring report quality and sector reporting patterns
Working with supervisors on reporting failures
Intended Audience: Operational and strategic analysts in financial intelligence units
FIU heads of analysis, team leaders and staff managing intake, dissemination and international cooperation
Investigators and liaison officers who request, receive or rely on FIU intelligence
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial intelligence, investigation or AML/CFT work is helpful. No specialist analytical or data science background is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
Egmont Group (2013), Principles for Information Exchange Between Financial Intelligence Units
Egmont Group (2013, as updated), Operational Guidance for FIU Activities and the Exchange of Information
FATF (2013, as updated), Methodology for Assessing Technical Compliance with the FATF Recommendations and the Effectiveness of AML/CFT Systems
